evidence.quote: Borrowed from {{bor|en|de|strollen}}, seemingly from {{uder|en|gsw|strollen}}; related to {{m|de|Strolch||vagabond; rascal}} and {{m|de|strolchen}}.

"roam, wander without a home" (a sense now obsolete); 1670s, "walk in a careless way,… See origin and meaning of stroll. from the Continent, perhaps from dialectal German strollen , a variant of Swiss German strolchen "to stroll about, loaf," from Strolch "vagabond, vagrant," also "fortuneteller," which is perhaps from Italian astrologo "astrologer.
